meta.day_selection: Two ordinary quantile days and two highest actual-rate days, selected retrospectively for contrasting replay; overlapping2h labels weight schedule counts. No model tuning uses this selection.
meta.edge_definition: Focal scheduled directed departures in next 2h; visualization aggregates both directions.

scenarios.resource_description: 4 hypothetical teams; at most 2 per airport. Each serves up to 2 scheduled legs and removes at most 15 minutes from the external delay floor; aircraft readiness remains binding.
scenarios.note: Fixed 16:00 UTC scenario, independent of the replay cursor. Denominator: all WN domestic completed legs scheduled in the following 8h; resources are restricted to eight focal airports. Baseline replay MAE on this day: 10.3 min across 1,972 completed flights. Full held-out replay late15 recall: 11.2%; tail events are poorly represented. Actual-tail topology uses hindsight; no cancellation recovery, causal savings or airline staffing claim.

models.summary: Frozen October–December holdout; 2h departure-disruption rate. tabular was selected using August/September validation. Graph versus temporal residual MAE reduction: +0.175 percentage points. This small/descriptive comparison is not a broad superiority claim. Calibration and 7-day block-bootstrap uncertainty are in the model report.

findings.title: Disruption differs within the same carrier network
findings.question: Which focal airports had the highest and lowest 2023 disruption rates?
findings.denominator: 555,335 WN departures from eight focal airports; denominator excludes unknown noncancelled departure status.
findings.finding: DEN recorded 35.9% late15-or-cancelled departures (96,164 scheduled), versus 22.1% at HOU (50,884).
findings.limitation: One carrier and reporting year; route mix, schedule and weather differ. This ranking does not measure airport management quality.
findings.decision: Use airport-specific baselines and compare within cohorts before allocating hypothetical resources.

findings.title: Aircraft continuity marks association, not cause
findings.question: Is a late inbound associated with a delayed next departure on validated aircraft chains?
findings.denominator: 1,160,285 immediate, validated same-tail domestic pairs with observed inbound and outbound delays; cancelled/diverted/gapped chains excluded.
findings.finding: Next departures were late15 in 80.4% of pairs after a late15 inbound, versus 14.0% after an inbound under15 minutes late.
findings.limitation: Retrospective actual tails, shared weather/airport conditions, selection on completed legs and missing international legs prevent a causal interpretation.
findings.decision: Use validated chains to investigate plausible propagation and test simulator assumptions; keep final tails out of forecasts.

findings.title: Averages conceal long tails and missing outcomes
findings.question: How much information is lost by reducing delay to a mean or filling missing arrival delays with zero?
findings.denominator: 1,438,465 deduplicated WN scheduled flights with departure-time checks passed; percentiles use non-null departure delay only.
findings.finding: Departure delay median was 1 min, mean 11.7 min, and 99th percentile 147 min. 592,247 departures were early; 17,227 arrival delays were unobserved.
findings.limitation: Cancelled and diverted flights censor arrival delay; extreme delays contribute heavily to the mean. No passenger-weighted effect is available.
findings.decision: Preserve signed early departures, report tails and cancellations alongside delay, and leave missing arrival outcomes null.

findings.title: Weather is useful context with confounding
findings.question: How does departure disruption differ under recorded higher-wind conditions?
findings.denominator: 24,140 focal departures with latest available wind ≥8 m/s, versus 524,184 other observed-weather departures; visibility <3km has a separate cohort.
findings.finding: Higher-wind cohort disruption was 41.2%, versus 28.8% in the other-observed cohort.
findings.limitation: As-of hourly observations assume 60-minute latency; QC-filtered readings can be absent. Airport, season and traffic confound the association.
findings.decision: Include observed weather as a forecast feature, then judge incremental performance on future dates rather than treating association as causal.

findings.title: The carrier scope is a deliberate selection
findings.question: How much of the January reporting-carrier traffic at the focal airports does the WN study cover?
findings.denominator: 80,786 scheduled departures in the January2023BTS reporting-carrier extract at the eight focal origins, including cancellations.
findings.finding: WN accounts for 43,468 of those departures (53.8%). The remaining reporting carriers have different airport, route and schedule mixes.
findings.limitation: January only; selected reporting carriers and origins, not all US operations or passenger market share. The comparison cannot isolate an airline effect.
findings.decision: Interpret the forecast as WN-network evidence and check carrier/airport composition before transferring findings to a different operation.
